chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى هِشَامُ بْنُ سَالِمٍ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ قَالَ لِرَجُلٍ يَا ابْنَ الْفَاعِلَةِ يَعْنِي الزِّنَا فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَتْ أُمُّهُ حَيَّةً شَاهِدَةً ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ تَطْلُبُ حَقَّهَا ضُرِبَ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ غَائِبَةً انْتُظِرَ بِهَا حَتَّى تَقْدَمَ فَتَطْلُبَ حَقَّهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ قَدْ مَاتَتْ وَ لَمْ يُعْلَمْ مِنْهَا إِلَّا خَيْرٌ ضُرِبَ الْمُفْتَرِي عَلَيْهَا الْحَدَّ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً».

translations.en: Regarding a man who said to another man, “O son of an adulteress,” meaning zinā. So he عليه السلام said: “If his mother is alive and present, then she comes and claims her right, he is to be struck eighty lashes. If she is absent, it is awaited for her until she arrives and claims her right. And if she has died, and nothing is known of her except goodness, the one who falsely accused her is to be given the hadd, eighty lashes.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on slanderous accusation against a person's mother through an insult implying zinā. It establishes that the hadd is carried out when the right is claimed by the living mother, deferred if she is absent, and still applicable after her death if she was known only for goodness.
en.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if someone calls another person the son of an adulteress?

key_terms.حَقَّهَا: her legal claim or personal right in the case
key_terms.غَائِبَةً: absent, requiring delay until her return
key_terms.الْمُفْتَرِي: the one who makes the false accusation
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes as the fixed punishment
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: good character and chastity known about the deceased woman
